title: MASAI Randomized Controlled Trial (105,934 Women) Proves AI Mammography Boosts Sensitivity and Cuts Aggressive Interval Cancers
aiSystem: Transpara AI Mammography Triage & Detection (MASAI Trial / Lund University)
whyItMatters: Published in The Lancet, the first population-based breast-AI RCT (105,934 women) proved AI-supported mammography raised sensitivity (80.5% vs 73.8%), lowered aggressive interval cancers, and cut radiologist workload with equal specificity.
summary: Published in The Lancet on January 31, 2026 (Vol. 407, Issue 10527, pp. 505–514, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(25)02464-X, PMID 41620232), Jessie Gommers, Kristina Lång, and colleagues at Lund University, Skåne University Hospital, and Radboudumc reported the primary-outcome results of MASAI (NCT04838756)—the first population-based randomized controlled trial of AI-supported mammography screening. Across 105,934 women randomly assigned 1:1 in Sweden’s national screening program, AI triaged exams to single or double radiologist reading and provided detection support. Compared with standard double reading without AI, AI-supported screening met its primary non-inferiority endpoint with a lower overall interval cancer rate (1.55 vs 1.76 per 1,000 participants; proportion ratio 0.88), produced fewer invasive (75 vs 89), T2+ (38 vs 48), and non-luminal A (43 vs 59) interval cancers, significantly raised cancer detection sensitivity (80.5% vs 73.8%, p = 0.031) across ages and breast densities, maintained identical 98.5% specificity, and substantially reduced screen-reading workload.
technicalHighlights: First population-based randomized controlled trial of AI in breast cancer screening (105,934 women, NCT04838756), establishing gold-standard clinical outcome evidence.
Increased screening sensitivity from 73.8% to 80.5% (p = 0.031) at identical 98.5% specificity while reducing radiologist screen-reading workload.
Achieved non-inferior, lower interval cancer rates (1.55 vs 1.76 per 1,000) with fewer invasive (75 vs 89), T2+ (38 vs 48), and non-luminal A (43 vs 59) missed cancers.
caveats: Single-country Swedish screening program using one commercial AI platform; while interval cancers declined descriptively, the trial was powered for non-inferiority (p = 0.41 for superiority on overall interval cancer rate).

scoreRationale.foundational: Crosses the clinical-evidence chasm from retrospective AI imaging benchmarks to a 105,934-patient randomized controlled trial with hard 2-year interval-cancer outcomes.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly informs national cancer-screening policy across Europe and globally, easing radiologist shortages while detecting more aggressive tumors early.
scoreRationale.verification: Gold-standard single-blinded, population-based randomized controlled trial (NCT04838756) published in The Lancet.
scoreRationale.velocity: AI triage nearly halved radiologist reading workload in routine clinical practice while improving sensitivity.
